clue.text: Cancel bad debt immediately we hear of it

indicators.note: we hear of it says the phrase is judged by its sound when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: immediately means right off, at once

explanation.surface: An accountant decides to cancel a bad debt the moment news of it arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear of it' signals a sound-alike: RIGHT OFF, meaning at once, is said the same as the accounting term.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon an unrecoverable loan in the books is to treat it as a loss, the accountant's phrase for this.

clue.text: Judgment of Dr West upheld poor Sid

indicators.note: poor shows the letters of Sid are in a bad state, rearranged
upheld in a down clue lifts the doctor upwards, so his letters read bottom to top

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor called West thinks a hard-up man named Sid shows judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SID to ISD; 'upheld' turns MO into OM; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is sound judgment, good sense.

clue.text: King's one to upset the state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to upset in a down clue tips the king's name over so it reads upwards

parts.note: Lear's: Shakespeare's King Lear, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A king's subject sets out to overthrow the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upset' turns LEARS into SRAEL, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a country in the Middle East, a nation state.

clue.text: Suitable contrivance

definitions.meaning: fitting or advisable for a purpose
a device or means to an end

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'contrivance', singular, which fits the noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means convenient or advisable; as a noun it is a makeshift device or means.

clue.text: Rodent moving by moonlight ?

parts.note: a mouse-like creature that flits about at night

explanation.walkthrough: A bat is not truly a rodent; the old name pictures it as a fluttering mouse, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the bat, which flits about at night and looks like a mouse with wings.

clue.text: Maltreats a lot of vehicles

parts.note: buses are a lot of vehicles, several public transport ones

explanation.surface: Someone is cruel to a whole fleet of cars and lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to misuse or harm, a verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: A good sort of builder ?

parts.note: a good sort of person, and something a builder lays

explanation.walkthrough: In old British slang a reliable, good-hearted person is 'a brick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable, kind person is called this in British slang, and builders lay these baked clay blocks.

clue.text: Miss girl after one's returned

indicators.note: after places the girl's name behind the turned word
returned means the word is sent back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ones, the possessive read as a plain word
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl comes after someone has come back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ONES into SENO; 'after' puts RITA behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Would roses need it ? Yes, in time

indicators.note: in places the word for yes inside the season

parts.note: spring is a time of year
ay is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether roses need something and answers yes, in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: AY goes inside SPRING after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are sprayed against greenfly and blight, so a spraying is what they would need.

clue.text: Odd phrase--" I'm in good spirits"!

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of phrase are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the strange expression 'I'm in good spirits'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges PHRASE to SERAPH; add IM and 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, so they are good spirits in the heavenly sense.

clue.text: One who secures a place on the 14 line?

definitions.meaning: someone who fastens things with pins
a station in north-west London on the Underground line named in 14 across

explanation.walkthrough: The 14 refers to the answer at 14 across, a London Underground line; this suburb is one of its stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastener with pins does the securing, and a London suburb with a station on that Underground line bears the same name.

clue.text: Gives food and training where services are needed in the palace

parts.note: ham is a meat
PT is physical training
gives as in puts on, so the ON of putting on a meal or class
a tennis court, where players serve

explanation.surface: A grand residence offers meals and exercise, and needs plenty of staff service.
explanation.walkthrough: To give food and training is to put on HAM and PT, so ON follows them; services are tennis serves, needed on a COURT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampton Court is a Tudor royal palace on the Thames near London.

clue.text: Nymph exhorts us to peruse mining camp notice

definitions.meaning: a mountain nymph of Greek myth
read as the cry '...!' urging us to look at a text
split as ore plus ad, an advertisement where minerals are dug

explanation.walkthrough: Three readings of one word: the nymph, the cry 'O, read!', and ORE AD, an advertisement at a mining camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain spirit of Greek legend bears this name; split up, it also sounds like a call to read and like a miners' advert.

clue.text: Writer wrecked a ketch, going to fish

indicators.note: a wrecked boat is broken up, so the letters of a ketch are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: An author smashes up a sailing boat while out fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges A KETCH to THACKE; 'going to' joins on RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was a Victorian novelist, author of Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Bishop encountered poor Latin translation

parts.note: encountered means met

indicators.note: translation turns the words into a new form, here the letters of poor Latin rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman came across a bad rendering of a Latin text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges the nine letters of POOR LATIN into ROPOLITAN; 'poor' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolitan is an archbishop presiding over a church province, a senior bishop.

clue.text: Picture the decoration on a piano, in a way

indicators.note: in places the decoration and the piano inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
DSC is the Distinguished Service Cross, a military decoration
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A painting of the ornament on a piano, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: DSC sits on A and P, and the lot goes in LANE after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of countryside scenery.

clue.text: Ready money-in marks ?

parts.note: money paid straight away, pictured as cash in the form of marks or dots

explanation.walkthrough: Spots are marks, so cash 'in marks' is cash in spots; the dash and question mark flag the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment on the spot is immediate payment in money, so ready money.

clue.text: Makes Dora go in for dance music

indicators.note: makes as in remakes or forms anew, so the letters of Dora go in are put together differently

explanation.surface: Someone persuades Dora to take up a dance tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' rearranges DORA GO IN; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively old French dance for couples, and the music for it.

clue.text: Race provides one example in Eton

parts.note: the word Eton is E, then TO, then N: a compass point, to, another compass point

explanation.surface: A school sport supposedly offers one case of it at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: E and N are compass points, so ETON spells 'point TO point'; 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is a cross-country steeplechase for amateur riders on hunting horses.

clue.text: It's tongue, of course — about a quarter

indicators.note: about means the course goes round the other letters

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A remark on a language, naturally, and a fraction of something.
explanation.walkthrough: DISH goes 'about' A and N; 'of' is a link. 'of course' looks like a phrase but 'course' alone is the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish is the language of Denmark, a tongue.

clue.text: State takes on an ensign

parts.note: Penn. is short for Pennsylvania, a US state

explanation.surface: A government decides to take on a junior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link joining PENN and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, a banner or ensign.

clue.text: Marine gives new hat to girl in charge

indicators.note: new means the letters of hat take a fresh order

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A soldier at sea gives a fresh hat to the girl who is in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges HAT to THA; then LASS and IC follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalassic is an adjective for things of the sea, from the Greek word for sea.

clue.text: Some small oast-houses in Scotland?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few little hop kilns are found north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in smALL OAst-houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the Forth in central Scotland.

clue.text: Colourful ghost'?

parts.note: the word for a ghost is also the word for a tint of colour

explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a spirit or phantom, and a tint of a colour shares the same name.

clue.text: Breathless greeting includes river god

indicators.note: includes means the greeting holds the river inside it
breathless drops the H, the breathy sound at the start of the greeting

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
the Po is a river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: Someone panting says hello to a river deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathless' drops the aspirate H from HALLO to leave ALLO, which 'includes' PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman deity of the sun, music and poetry.

clue.text: Native rugger-player meets Scot

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, the game called rugger
a man is a player in a team or a piece in a game
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A local rugby man has an encounter with someone from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rugger-player' splits into RU and MAN; 'meets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Romania, in the older spelling of the country's name.

clue.text: Girl returns by herself

indicators.note: the name read in return, backwards, gives itself unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A young woman comes home alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns by herself' says the name read backwards is still the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannah is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Love-sick shepherd collects shop rent

indicators.note: collects means the letters of shop rent are gathered up and put together afresh

explanation.surface: A lovelorn farmhand gathers in the rent from his shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' gathers the letters of SHOP RENT and rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Strephon is the lovesick shepherd of Sidney's Arcadia, and the Arcadian shepherd in Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe.
